arxiv-1602-04696.title: Bound State Operators and Wedge-Locality in Integrable Quantum Field Theories
arxiv-1602-04696.creator: Yoh TANIMOTO †‡
arxiv-1602-04696.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Yoh TANIMOTO †‡. We consider scalar two-dimensional quantum field theories with a factorizing S S -matrix which has poles in the physical strip. In our previous work, we introduced the bound state operators and constructed candidate operators for observables in wedges. Under some additional assumptions on the S S -matrix, we show that, in order to obtain their strong commutativity, it is enough to prove the essential self-adjointness of the sum of the left and right bound state operators.

arxiv-2103-14654.title: Full sky Integrated Sachs-Wolfe maps for the MICE Grand Challenge lightcone simulation 2020 Full sky Integrated Sachs-Wolfe maps for the MICE Grand Challenge lightcone simulation – References
arxiv-2103-14654.creator: Krishna Naidoo, Pablo Fosalba, Lorne Whiteway, Ofer Lahav
arxiv-2103-14654.description: Abstract We present full-sky maps of the Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect (ISW) for the MICE Grand Challenge lightcone simulation up to redshift 1.4 1.4 . The maps are constructed in the linear regime using spherical Bessel transforms. We compare and contrast this procedure against analytical approximations found in the literature.

arxiv-2207-02517.title: Transaction Monitoring of Smart Contracts
arxiv-2207-02517.creator: Margarita Capretto, Martin Ceresa, César Sánchez
arxiv-2207-02517.description: Abstract Blockchains are modern distributed systems that provide decentralized financial capabilities with trustable guarantees. Smart contracts are programs written in specialized programming languages running on a blockchain and govern how tokens and cryptocurrency are sent and received. Smart contracts can invoke other contracts during the execution of transactions initiated by external users.

arxiv-2303-01562.title: Quantum State Preparation of Normal Distributions using Matrix Product States
arxiv-2303-01562.creator: Jason Iaconis, Sonika Johri, Elton Yechao Zhu
arxiv-2303-01562.description: Abstract State preparation is a necessary component of many quantum algorithms. In this work, we combine a method for efficiently representing smooth differentiable probability distributions using matrix product states with recently discovered techniques for initializing quantum states to approximate matrix product states.

arxiv-2305-02194.title: Generalized hypergeometric coherent states for special functions: mathematical and physical properties
arxiv-2305-02194.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . In continuation of our previous works [ J. 35 , 9355-9365 (2002)], [ J. 38 , 7851 (2005)] and [ Eur. D 72 , 172 (2018)], we investigate a class of generalized coherent states for associated Jacobi polynomials and hypergeometric functions, satisfying the resolution of the identity with respect to a weight function expressed in terms of Meijer’s G-function. We extend the state Hilbert space of the constructed states and discuss the property of the reproducing kernel and its analytical expansion.

arxiv-2306-08348.title: Generative deep-learning reveals collective variables of Fermionic systems
arxiv-2306-08348.creator: Raphaël-David Lasseri, David Regnier, Mikaël Frosini, Marc Verriere, Nicolas Schunck
arxiv-2306-08348.description: Abstract Complex processes ranging from protein folding to nuclear fission often follow a low-dimension reaction path parameterized in terms of a few collective variables. In nuclear theory, variables related to the shape of the nuclear density in a mean-field picture are key to describing the large amplitude collective motion of the neutrons and protons.

arxiv-2312-16339.title: Universal Pyramid Adversarial Training for Improved ViT Performance
arxiv-2312-16339.creator: Ping-yeh Chiang, Yipin Zhou, Omid Poursaeed, Satya Narayan Shukla, Ashish Shah, Tom Goldstein, Ser-Nam Lim
arxiv-2312-16339.description: Abstract Recently, Pyramid Adversarial training ( Herrmann et al. 2022 ) has been shown to be very effective for improving clean accuracy and distribution-shift robustness of vision transformers. However, due to the iterative nature of adversarial training, the technique is up to 7 times more expensive than standard training.

arxiv-2503-11969.title: Evaluation of Intra-operative Patient-specific Methods for Point Cloud Completion for Minimally Invasive Liver Interventions
arxiv-2503-11969.creator: Nakul Poudel, Zixin Yang, Kelly Merrell, Richard Simon, Cristian A. Linte
arxiv-2503-11969.description: Abstract The registration between the pre-operative model and the intra-operative surface is crucial in image-guided liver surgery, as it facilitates the effective use of pre-operative information during the procedure. However, the intra-operative surface, usually represented as a point cloud, often has limited coverage, especially in laparoscopic surgery, and is prone to holes and noise, posing significant challenges for registration methods.

arxiv-2504-17999.title: Streaming, Fast and Slow: Cognitive Load-Aware Streaming for Efficient LLM Serving
arxiv-2504-17999.creator: Chang Xiao, Brenda Z. Yang
arxiv-2504-17999.description: Abstract . Generative conversational interfaces powered by large language models (LLMs) typically stream output token-by-token at a rate determined by computational budget, often neglecting actual human reading speeds and the cognitive load associated with the content. This mismatch frequently leads to inefficient use of computational resources.

arxiv-2510-00534.title: Photonic Hybrid Quantum Computing
arxiv-2510-00534.creator: Jaehak Lee, Srikrishna Omkar, Yong Siah Teo, Seok-Hyung Lee, Hyukjoon Kwon, M. S. Kim, Hyunseok Jeong
arxiv-2510-00534.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jaehak Lee, Srikrishna Omkar, Yong Siah Teo, Seok-Hyung Lee, Hyukjoon Kwon, M. S. Kim, Hyunseok Jeong. SUMMARY Photons are a ubiquitous carrier of quantum information: they are fast, suffer minimal decoherence, and do not require huge cryogenic facilities. Nevertheless, their intrinsically weak photon–photon interactions remain a key obstacle to scalable quantum computing.

arxiv-2510-01582.title: ImageNet-Think-250K: A Large-Scale Synthetic Dataset for Multimodal Reasoning for Vision Language Models
arxiv-2510-01582.creator: Krishna Teja Chitty-Venkata, Murali Emani
arxiv-2510-01582.description: Abstract We develop ImageNet-Think, a multimodal reasoning dataset designed to aid the development of Vision Language Models (VLMs) with explicit reasoning capabilities. Our dataset is built on 250,000 images from ImageNet-21k dataset, providing structured thinking tokens and corresponding answers. Our synthetic dataset is generated by two state-of-the-art VLMs: GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking and Kimi-VL-A3B-Thinking-2506.

arxiv-2511-01042.title: A sensitivity analysis of interstellar ice chemistry in astrochemical models
arxiv-2511-01042.creator: Tobias M. Dijkhuis ,, Thanja Lamberts ,, Serena Viti, Herma M. Cuppen
arxiv-2511-01042.description: Abstract Context. Astrochemical models are essential to bridge the gap between the timescales of reactions, experiments, and observations. Ice chemistry in these models experiences a large computational complexity as a result of the many parameters required for the modeling of chemistry occurring on these ices, such as binding energies and reaction energy barriers.

pmc-10572912.creator: Nadia Muhammad Hussain, Bilal Amin, Martin O’Halloran, Adnan Elahi, Xavier Muñoz-Berbel
pmc-10572912.description: Asphyxia, a leading cause of illness and death in newborns, can be improved by early detection and management. Arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis is commonly used to diagnose and manage asphyxia, but it is invasive and carries risks. Dermal interstitial fluid (ISF) is an alternative physiological fluid that can provide valuable information about a person’s health.

pmc-11494864.creator: Dhanusha Punyadasa, Nicola J Adderley, Gavin Rudge, Prasad Nagakumar, Shamil Haroon
pmc-11494864.description: BackgroundThe indoor home environment plays a crucial role in determining the outcome of respiratory diseases, including asthma. pmc-12655299.description: Momordica charantia L. (Cucurbitaceae) has been widely recognized for its pharmacological potential, although studies on its leaves remain scarce. pmc-12658252.title: Isolation, characterization, and bioremediation potential of oil-degrading bacteria from contaminated soils in Shiraz and Bandar Abbas, Iran
pmc-12658252.creator: Sara Shokranian, Morteza Yousefzadi, Narges Amrollahi Biuki, Mohammad Yaghoubi-Avini, Majedeh TaheriAkerdi
pmc-12658252.description: Petroleum hydrocarbons are among the most persistent environmental pollutants, posing serious risks to soil and aquatic ecosystems. Bioremediation using indigenous hydrocarbon-degrading bacteria provides a cost-effective and environmentally sustainable alternative to physical and chemical treatments. In this study, oil-degrading bacteria were isolated from contaminated soils collected near oil refineries in Shiraz and Bandar Abbas, Iran, and screened for their biodegradation potential.
